data.narrative:
Itera is a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by AJ Cooper (PhD EE, ex-Uber Jump/Lyft hardware), Mattis Fjällström (ex-Verkada), and Alex Withrow (ex-Bridgewater/VMware). The company has raised $12M to date. The Chips & Semiconductors sector includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers such as Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, Etched, and Ayar Labs.

Of three valuation methods examined, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method applies a typical Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x against the $12M total raised as a proxy for current value, yielding $30M. Peer-Median comparison was not viable: while 13 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three datapoints fell into sufficiently narrow cohorts (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier), making sector-wide medians unrepresentative. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied because Itera's revenue is not on file; the sector median P/S of 18.9x across the three public tickers is not actionable without this input.

The triangulated valuation range is $26M–$34M, with a median of $30M. This analysis rests on a single method and is therefore sensitive to stage-progression assumptions. Key uncertainties include the appropriate step-up multiplier for this particular seed cohort, the eventual revenue trajectory, and whether the founder team's hardware and operations background translates to defensible IP in a crowded sector.
